text:
maria (Support): hey team, escalating a customer issue. Kevin from Acme started getting lots of 429s after they increased context from ~4k tokens to ~16k and switched to bursty batches (20 reqs / sec for ~30s). They say responses sometimes return JSON with "code": "model_rate_limit" and occasionally "context_throttle". Sample error from their app:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Request rate exceeded",
    "type": "rate_limit",
    "code": "model_rate_limit",
    "retry_after": 12
  }
}
```

Repro steps provided by customer:
1) model: redwood-large-16k (they call it "rwl-large-16k")
2) send 20 concurrent requests in bursts (each request ~16k context + 512 gen)
3) environment: hosted api, region us-west1, using our JS SDK v0.9.2
4) they get 200 OK most of time but ~15% of requests return 429s across the burst window

Can someone check if this is a per-model RPM/TPM or concurrency cap? Also need an internal explanation to send back + recommendations.

kevin (Customer): adding exact curl they used:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXXXX" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large-16k","input":"<huge prompt here>","max_tokens":512}'
```

alex (SRE): thanks, putting this on my queue. A few quick checks we should run:
- confirm model-specific RPM/TPM and concurrency defaults for redwood-large-16k
- look at rate-limiter logs and the "retry_after" values to see whether it's token-based throttling or request-count throttling
- check grafana: dashboard "api.ratelimiter" and the per-model panel for last 1h

Run these from infra (examples):
```bash
# admin endpoint (internal)
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" "https://admin.internal/redwood/limits?customer_id=acct_ABC123&model=redwood-large-16k"

# search logs for trace id if present (replace TRACEID)
rg "TRACEID" /var/log/redwood | head -n 200
kubectl logs -l app=ratelimiter -n prod | rg "acct_ABC123" | tail -n 200
```

ben (Platform): quick note on defaults: redwood-large-16k currently has default soft-limits of ~1200 RPM and 50k TPM for hosted customers, with a max concurrency of 12 per API key (these are soft and vary by tier). Important math to call out to customer: tokens_per_request * requests_per_minute hits TPM. If they go from 4k->16k context, that's ~4x tokens per request -> their effective tokens/minute can spike and hit TPM even if RPM remains under the request-count cap.

example: 20 rps sustained for 30s = 1200 requests in a minute; if each request uses 16k tokens that's 19.2M tokens/min which far exceeds a 50k TPM limit (so they'll get token-throttle, not request-count throttle). For short bursts the burst window matters; we allow small short bursts but not sustained token floods.

sara (Engineer): good candidate mitigations to propose to Acme:
- enable prefix/KV caching so they don't re-send the full history each time (store encoded context and reuse)
- switch to delta updates or only send new messages rather than entire context
- stream generation so client can early-abort when not needed
- reduce batch size or add client-side pacing/backoff (exponential jitter)
- request a temporary TPU/Tokens bump (we can increase TPM for paid accounts or propose Dedicated nodes)

I can paste a small snippet for KV cache pattern they can implement quickly:
```js
// pseudocode: keep encoded prefix and only send new tokens
const prefix = await encodeAndStore(contextHead);
const prompt = buildPrompt({ prefixReference: prefix.id, tail: newUserMessages });
await api.generate({ model: 'redwood-large-16k', input: prompt });
```

alex (SRE): also check whether they hit per-model concurrency (12). The SDK will open many sockets; if they open more than concurrency cap, we'll queue/throttle at edge causing head-of-line delays and 429s. Ask customer to throttle concurrency to 8 and see if 429 rate drops.

maria (Support): I pulled an admin limits response for acct_ABC123 (scrubbed) — shows: `{
  "model": "redwood-large-16k",
  "rpm_soft": 1200,
  "tpm_soft": 50000,
  "concurrency": 12,
  "burst_window_s": 60
}`

alex (SRE): looks like token budget explains it. Next actions:
- ben: confirm whether we enforce context-length specific throttles (we have a per-request token cap + token-budget enforcement; sometimes the error surfaces as "context_throttle" when the token footprint is anomalous)
- I'll pull grafana panels + rate-limiter logs and paste screenshots
- maria: ask customer for a trace id or attach one into a repro so we can correlate logs

ben (Platform): confirmed — we have a soft per-request token ceiling at 20k tokens and token-budget enforcement (TPM) that will start returning 429s with code "context_throttle" or "model_rate_limit" depending on which limiter fired. We also have a short burst allowance controlled by "burst_window_s" and "burst_tokens" which is tuned per tier.

deploy-bot: rollout redwood/ratelimiter v2.3.7 to prod/us-west1 at 2026-03-14T16:12:00Z :white_check_mark:

maria (Support): summary for customer reply (draft):
- root cause: increase in tokens-per-request (16k contexts) pushed their workload past hosted TPM soft limits; some requests also hit per-key concurrency limits during bursty windows
- immediate mitigations: reduce concurrency to <=8, add client-side pacing, use prefix/KV caching, reduce context size where possible
- medium term: request increased token quota (we can propose +100k TPM temporary bump) or move to Dedicated for predictable capacity
- debug steps: please capture a trace id for any 429 and share it; we checked limits and logs and confirmed token-based throttling

Action items:
- ben: confirm exact burst_tokens & burst_window for acct_ABC123 and whether we can grant a short window bump (ETA 2 business days)
- alex: paste grafana + logs (ETA 2h)
- sara: write short KB on KV/prefix caching and a tiny code sample (ETA EOD)

kevin (Customer): thanks, trying the concurrency cap reduction now and will send trace ids if we still hit 429s.

maria (Support): thanks — I'll keep this thread updated and attach logs/screenshots when alex/ben provide them.
